summary: Defines MIB objects for managing multiple logical and physical entities, such as chassis, cards and modules, within a single SNMP agent. It is a standards-track document at the proposed standard level, and it was replaced by RFC 4133.

eli5.summary: A network box has many parts inside. This gives management software a way to list every part and how they fit.

questions: how to list physical components via snmp
subtitle: A MIB that lets one SNMP agent describe the physical parts and logical entities inside a single managed box.

tldr.problem: A single SNMP agent can manage several logical entities, such as multiple bridges or OSPF instances, inside one physical device, and management stations need a standard way to see which exist and which hardware they use.
tldr.mechanism: The Entity MIB defines tables of physical entities arranged in a containment hierarchy, a table of logical entities, mapping tables that tie them together, and a change timestamp with a notification.
tldr.outcome: Version 2 adds admin-assigned identifiers, revision and vendor attributes and SNMPv3 context support. It is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 4133.

today: RFC 2737 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 4133, so use that RFC for the current Entity MIB. It had replaced RFC 2037.

sections.title: Why an Entity MIB
sections.content:
Some devices run several instances of one MIB under one agent. The RFC gives three examples: multiple bridges in one device, multiple repeaters under one agent, and multiple OSPF backbone areas inside a router, each in its own Autonomous System and each using the same area-id such as 0.0.0.0. Something must tell a management station which logical entities exist and let it address one of them.

Version 2 answers new needs. These are non-volatile, administratively assigned identifiers for physical components, alignment with the SNMPv3 administrative framework in RFC 2571, and extra attributes that implementation experience showed to be useful.

The RFC states what the MIB is not. It is not a replacement for a Chassis MIB, since an earlier IETF working group that tried to define one reached no consensus. Most objects are read-only on purpose, though version 2 lets an administrator configure a few attributes of physical components.
sections.eli5: Imagine one big building with several small shops inside, all answered by a single receptionist. The receptionist needs a directory that says which shops exist and where they sit.

sections.title: Physical, Logical and Naming Scope Terms
sections.content:
A physical entity is an identifiable physical resource such as a port, backplane, sensor, daughter-card, power supply or the whole chassis. Which ones an agent lists is up to the implementation. A logical entity is something like a router, bridge or print server that is represented by at most one instance of a set of MIB objects. Zero or more logical entities may use a given physical entity.

The containment tree records where a component sits. Each physical entity points to the one that contains it through entPhysicalContainedIn, and following those links upward ends at a value of zero.

A naming scope is the set of information reachable through one SNMP operation, sharing one identifier space. For SNMPv1 it is identified by entLogicalCommunity, and for SNMPv3 the term is context. A multi-scoped object has the same instance value mean different things in different scopes, and a single-scoped object does not. The Entity MIB itself is single-scoped.
sections.eli5: Physical things are the real pieces you could hold, like cards and fans. Logical things are the jobs the box does, like acting as a router. A tree shows which piece sits inside which.

sections.title: The Five Groups of Objects
sections.content:
The MIB has five groups. The entityPhysical group holds entPhysicalTable with one row per physical entity, and it always has at least one row for an overall entity of class stack(11), chassis(3) or module(9). Rows carry a description, vendor type, class, containment link and position, plus version 2 additions: hardware, firmware and software revisions, serial number, manufacturer and model names, and an FRU flag.

Three strings can be written by a management station. entPhysicalAlias is a non-volatile identifier, entPhysicalAssetID is a user asset identifier for removable parts, and entPhysicalSerialNum is writable in case the agent cannot discover serial numbers.

The entityLogical group holds entLogicalTable, with a name, description and type for each logical entity and the information needed to reach it, including the SNMPv3 entLogicalContextEngineID and entLogicalContextName. It must be implemented if an agent represents several logical entities in different scopes.

The entityMapping group has three tables: entLPMappingTable ties logical to physical entities, entAliasMappingTable links entities to identifiers in other MIBs such as interface or repeater ports, and entPhysicalContainsTable lets a manager quickly find all children of a container. The entityGeneral group has entLastChangeTime, and the notifications group covers status changes.
sections.eli5: There is a parts list, a jobs list, and two lists that connect parts to jobs. There is also a clock that says when anything last changed.

sections.title: Relationships to Other MIBs and Agents
sections.content:
The mapping table can identify the physical location of each interface in the Interfaces MIB ifTable and of each repeater port. entPhysicalName and entPhysicalAlias approximate ifName and ifAlias for every kind of physical component.

More than one agent can exist in a device, and instances of the Entity MIB from different agents are not required to be equivalent or even consistent. An agent that sees the whole modular device would typically give the top entry class chassis, while one that sees only its own module would use module. The logical table's address objects exist to support an older multiplexing mechanism and are not meant to point at other agents.

Version 2 also changed three objects from the obsolete DisplayString to SnmpAdminString. The authors admit this is not strictly supported by SMIv2 but judged deprecating and replacing the objects to be worse for compatibility. A bug fix widened the entLogicalCommunity subrange to 0..255 and deprecated that object.
sections.eli5: The parts list can point to entries in other lists, like the list of network plugs. If two receptionists each keep a list, the lists may not match exactly, and that is allowed.

sections.title: Usage Examples
sections.content:
Section 4 walks through two devices using a made-up vendor called Acme. The first is a router with a chassis, two slots and a 3-port module in each slot. It has two logical OSPF instances and two logical bridges. Each OSPF instance maps to one port, and each bridge maps to all the ports on one module.

The second is a repeater chassis with two Ethernet backplanes, three slots, and plug-in modules whose 10Base-T ports are modeled as separate physical entities. The examples show how entPhysicalContainedIn chains build the tree and how the tables describe real hardware.
sections.eli5: The examples are sample parts lists for two pretend boxes, showing how each card and plug is written down.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Read-write and read-create objects can be sensitive, and SET operations in an insecure environment can hurt network operations. Even read access can expose information: hardware, firmware and software revisions, serial numbers, and manufacturer and model names reveal what is in the system, while the logical table can expose community names, network addresses and SNMPv3 context details.

The RFC says to control even GET access and possibly to encrypt values in transit. It notes that SNMPv1 alone is not a secure environment, and recommends the SNMPv3 security features, specifically the User-based Security Model (RFC 2574) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2575).
sections.eli5: The parts list tells strangers exactly what is inside your box, which can help them plan an attack. So only trusted people should be allowed to read or change it.
